api_endpoint_security.intent: API endpoint security validation: public endpoints should validate input and sanitize outputs; production code must not expose internal error details

input_validation_missing.instructions: Does this file contain public API endpoints that handle user input without validation or sanitization?

criteria.true: A public API function/endpoint reads request parameters directly without validation (regex/email/integer checks, length limits) or sanitization (escape, stringify, parameter binding)
criteria.false: All public API endpoints have proper input validation (regex, type checks, length bounds) or use parameterized queries/ORM safe methods, or the endpoint is internal/private

output_sanitization_missing.instructions: Does this file contain public API endpoints that output data without proper sanitization?

criteria.true: A public API endpoint returns user-controlled data (query params, form data, path parameters) without escaping or sanitization, potentially enabling XSS or injection attacks
criteria.false: All API endpoints sanitize outputs (HTML escape, JSON encoding, proper content-type) or return only non-user data, or use template engines with auto-escaping

error_handling_exposure.instructions: Classify this file's error handling in public API endpoints.

criteria.safe: Errors are properly caught, logged internally, and return generic user-facing messages without internal details
criteria.risky: Errors expose stack traces, internal paths, database queries, or sensitive system information to users
criteria.not_api: File does not contain public API endpoints or uses error handling patterns appropriate for internal code

authentication_missing.instructions: Does this file contain API endpoints that should require authentication but don't validate any auth tokens?

criteria.true: A public API function/endpoint reads request data without checking authentication tokens, API keys, or other auth mechanisms where auth is required
criteria.false: All API endpoints either are explicitly public (marked @public) or properly validate authentication tokens/API keys/tokens
